issues.legal_issue: A land-acquisition reference court may decide a compensation-enhancement objection only if that objection has been referred to it, and cannot acquire jurisdiction over an un referred objection by converting an apportionment reference or relying on a later clarification.
material_facts: The land acquisition officer referred the dispute only to determine how compensation should be apportioned.
The reference letter did not mention a compensation-enhancement objection or name the claimant seeking enhancement as a party.
A later letter from the officer said that an application was attached to the file but had been omitted from the reference letter by error.
The reference court impleaded the claimant, treated the pending apportionment reference as also being a reference for enhancement, and enhanced the compensation.
issues.conclusion: There was no valid reference concerning enhancement of compensation. The later clarification could not constitute such a reference, and the reference court lacked jurisdiction to enhance compensation. The High Court correctly set aside the enhancement, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 18 and 30 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, a reference court obtains jurisdiction only over matters referred to it; Section 21 confines its inquiry to the referred objection. It cannot widen the reference or convert a reference for apportionment into one for enhancement. A statutory condition necessary to confer jurisdiction cannot be waived or cured by acquiescence. The Court relied on Pramatha Nath Mullick Bahadur v. Secretary of State, Mohammed Hasnuddin v. State of Maharashtra, K. Kankarathanamma v. State of Andhra Pradesh, and Ajjam Linganna v. Land Acquisition Officer, and cited the jurisdiction principle in Nusserwanjee Pestonjee v. Meer Mynoodeen Khan.

rule.if: land_acquisition_reference_proceeding and original_reference_limited_to_apportionment and no_compensation_objection_in_reference and claimant_not_named_in_reference and later_letter_claimed_application_was_attached and reference_court_enhanced_compensation

predicates.land_acquisition_reference_proceeding: The proceeding arose from a reference made in a land-acquisition matter.
predicates.original_reference_limited_to_apportionm: The land acquisition officer referred only a dispute about apportionment of compensation.
predicates.no_compensation_objection_in_reference: The reference did not identify an objection seeking enhancement of compensation.
predicates.claimant_not_named_in_reference: The claimant seeking enhancement was not named as a party in the reference.
predicates.later_letter_claimed_application_was_att: The land acquisition officer later said that an application had been attached to the file but omitted from the reference letter by error.
predicates.reference_court_enhanced_compensation: The reference court treated the matter as including an enhancement reference and increased compensation.

issues.definition: When a land-acquisition reference proceeding involves only an apportionment reference, contains no referred compensation objection, and the reference court nevertheless enhances compensation after a later letter claims an application was attached, the enhancement is without jurisdiction.
